Linh: Quick heads-up — after switching the reranker to PTQ int8 (ranker-v2, candidate set A) the eval shows ndcg@10 -2.3% but mrr@1 +0.5% vs fp32. Not expected. run id 2026-03-15_09:12_anchored. Anyone seen this head/tail divergence before?
Devon: Interesting. Did anything change in candidate curation or sampleweights for that run?
Linh: sampleweights unchanged. The only infra diff was: we enabled html-preserve on candidate preprocessing (we used to strip tags). Suspect tokenization shift or priming interaction.
Matt: Can you paste the eval-harness command and the exact diffs? Short queries often drive ndcg but also MRR.
Linh: Pasting the command we ran and the per-slice output we got:
```
# repro command
./eval_harness --model ranker-v2-int8 --candidates candidates_A.jsonl --holdout holdout_v2.jsonl --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@1 --seed 42 --preserve-html True

# summary diff (int8 vs fp32)
ndcg@10: -2.3%
mrr@1: +0.47%
short_queries (len<=8): ndcg@10 -4.6%
long_queries (len>50): ndcg@10 +0.2%
```
Eval-bot: automated rerun queued: job 2026-03-15-09:20. Interim results: confirms ndcg@10 -2.3, mrr@1 +0.47. Slice breakdown points at short queries and html-heavy candidates.
Katie: OK can we run a small ablation matrix:
  A) int8 scoring but fp32 priming (keep kv cache behavior)
  B) int8 + strip-html preproc (back to old behavior)
  C) preserve-order vs shuffled-candidates (to rule out nondet ordering)
Also include deterministic seed and identical batch sizes. I can kick off A/B/C on a small shard.
Devon: Also log token counts per candidate before and after preprocess. If HTML preservation adds tokens it could change attention windows and kvpack behavior.
Matt: Add another axis: run with and without prefix-cache enabled. That has bitten us before for short queries.
Linh: I'm running A+B now on a 10k sample. Command for token counts:
```
python -c "from token_utils import count_tokens; print(count_tokens(''.join(candidate['text'])))"
```
I'll post the CSV when done.
Katie: I'll take C and the prefix-cache toggle. ETA 3h.
Matt: Triage actions (owner): 1) run A/B (Katie/Linh) 2) token count diff (Linh) 3) prefix-cache ablation (Katie) 4) reproducibility (seed + ordering) (Devon) 5) if still repro, run fp32 scoring with new preproc to isolate quantization effect (Matt). Update in this thread when you have per-slice tables.
Linh: ack. If this narrows to html-preserve causing the shift we should consider normalizing tags before tokenization or limiting tag-length. Posting logs to the thread when available :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Eval-bot: job 2026-03-15-10:05 completed (A run): ndcg@10 delta -2.25, mrr@1 +0.48, token_count_mean short_queries +2.1 tokens when preserve-html=True.
Devon: Token bump small but could disproportionately affect short queries. Next step: normalize tags -> re-run short-query slice.
Katie: Starting normalization run now (strip attributes, keep text nodes). Will report slice CSV.
Linh: Thanks — sounds like a plausible path. If normalization fixes ndcg we can roll a preprocessing patch. If not, we'll dig deeper into quantization per-layer score noise.
Matt: Thanks team. Keep the thread lean. If anyone sees other odd slices (brand queries, paraphrase anchors) ping me directly.
